questions.prompt: Match each line shape on a distance–time graph to its meaning.
questions.explain: Slope = speed; flat = zero speed; downward = returning.

questions.prompt: A distance–time graph is a straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (5 s, 20 m). What is the speed?
Two straight lines start at the origin. Line A is steeper than line B. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: A steeper slope means more distance per second: faster.

questions.prompt: A graph is flat at 30 m from t = 10 s to t = 25 s. For how long was the object stopped?
questions.explain: 25 − 10 = 15 seconds with no change in distance.

questions.prompt: A graph shows: a gentle slope, then flat, then a steep slope. Put the story in order.
questions.explain: Gentle slope = slow; flat = stopped; steep = fast.

questions.prompt: On a distance–time graph, a line curves upwards and gets steeper and steeper. What is happening?

feedback.1: The graph shows distance over time, not the shape of the road!

questions.text: On a distance–time graph, time is plotted on the ___ axis. The slope of the line gives the ___.
questions.explain: Time on the x-axis; slope = speed.

questions.prompt: A cyclist goes from 400 m at t = 4 min to 1000 m at t = 6 min. What is the speed in m/min?
Describe the journey shown by this data: 0 min, 0 m; 2 min, 400 m; 4 min, 400 m; 6 min, 1000 m.
questions.modelAnswer: From 0 to 2 minutes the cyclist moved at a constant speed of 200 m/min. From 2 to 4 minutes they stopped (distance stayed at 400 m). From 4 to 6 minutes they moved faster, at 300 m/min, reaching 1000 m.
rubric: First stage: moving at constant speed (200 m/min)
questions.explain: Break the journey into stages and give the speed of each.
